learningObjective: Trace how a polynomial kernel replaces two explicit high-dimensional feature mappings and their dot product with one low-dimensional calculation that returns exactly the same scalar.
mediumRationale: A deterministic SVG is the smallest medium that can place the expensive explicit route and the kernel shortcut side by side, preserve their shared inputs and equal output, and attach a checkable degree-two numerical example to both paths.

pages.insight: Frames machine-learning algorithms as linear-algebra operations and uses the word kernel for Fourier and wavelet operators; this is useful neighboring context but a different use of kernel from a positive-semidefinite similarity function.

The dedicated Kernel trick panel states that a directly computed similarity can bypass an intractable feature map, identifies dot-product-only algorithms as the enabling condition, and mentions Gaussian kernels' infinite-dimensional feature space. It is the deck's closest treatment of the article's hardest mental model.

The immediately following Kernel PCA panel applies the substitution to a covariance-style computation, confirming how downstream algorithms consume feature-space relationships without explicit nonlinear coordinates.

The next slide broadens the idea to similarity matrices in clustering and Gaussian processes, where kernel values become an affinity or covariance matrix rather than an explicit feature representation.
The neighboring K-nearest-neighbor slide returns to explicit distance calculations and embedding-space comparisons, providing contrast with the kernel trick rather than another kernel construction.

The later Performer panel uses a feature-map approximation to reassociate attention products; it is relevant to the article's attention section but addresses explicit random features for scaling, not the exact classical shortcut.

deckReview.notes: All 214 pages of the local PDF were text-indexed page by page for kernel, kernel trick, feature space, support vector, SVM, similarity, Gram, Mercer, and positive-semidefinite terminology. Pages 20-24 were inspected as the complete immediate neighborhood around the sole dedicated classical kernel-trick treatment on page 21. Pages 29 and 36 only mention polynomial-kernel intuition in factorization machines and hinge loss in SVMs; pages 108 and 111 use kernel in the GPU or sparse-attention sense. Page 112 is the only later feature-map kernel mechanism. No deck image, wording, equation layout, code, coordinates, or visual composition is reused.

sourceReview.notes: The hardest prose-only mental model is that the trick does not approximate the feature-space inner product: for a valid kernel it evaluates exactly the same scalar while skipping both explicit feature vectors. The original example uses x = (2, 1), x' = (1, 3), and phi(z) = [z1^2, sqrt(2) z1 z2, z2^2, sqrt(2) z1, sqrt(2) z2, 1], for which phi(x) dot phi(x') = 4 + 12 + 9 + 4 + 6 + 1 = 36 and k(x, x') = (x dot x' + 1)^2 = (5 + 1)^2 = 36. The equality is algebraically exact. Path position, explicit route labels, a dashed bypass, and identical textual endpoints carry the lesson without color.

agentReview.summary: Read the complete article, text-indexed all 214 deck pages and inspected the exact kernel neighborhood plus the later attention treatment, then checked an authoritative SVM tutorial, a standard Gaussian-process textbook, official scikit-learn documentation, and source-licensing guidance before selecting an original exact-equivalence SVG.

implementation.accessibility: The SVG has a linked title and detailed description that narrate both routes, all inputs, the explicit six-term dot product, the direct kernel calculation, and their equal output. Route headings, line position, a dashed shortcut, equations, and duplicate 36 endpoints make meaning independent of color. A single 360-unit viewBox with no minimum width scales within the established plot-panel primitive at 390 CSS pixels; existing theme variables provide dark-mode contrast, and shared print rules switch to a light high-contrast palette and keep the figure together.
